strategy.bottleneck: The CUTLASS 3x3 conv (128x64x16 tile, split_k=1) is 86.6% of steady GPU time (844us/launch on the mid shape = 87% of TF32 peak) and only ~62% of peak on the 2x256x64x64 shape, where it emits just 256 CTAs for 170 SMs (1.5 waves).
strategy.optimisation method: Specialize the conv configuration per problem shape: instantiate a second, larger CUTLASS tile (128x128x16, warp 64x64x16) for shapes with enough CTAs, and enable serial split-k on the low-CTA shape so the grid covers >=2 full waves. Keep the current 128x64 config as fallback.
strategy.modification plan:
1. Keep every non-conv kernel (nchw2nhwc_round, weight_krsc_round, gn_partial, gn_finalize, gn_silu_round, gn_silu_add_nchw) and their launch shapes byte-for-byte unchanged; this round touches only the conv path.
2. Add a second instantiation of the existing MakeConv template: `using ConvBig = MakeConv<cutlass::gemm::GemmShape<128,128,16>, cutlass::gemm::GemmShape<64,64,16>, 4>::Op;` and keep `using ConvSmall = MakeConv<GemmShape<128,64,16>, GemmShape<64,32,16>, 4>::Op;`. Both stay ElementA/B = tfloat32_t, ElementAcc = float, Sm80 OpClassTensorOp, InstructionShape 16x8x8, LinearCombination<float,4>, kOptimized, alignment 4/4 (C=K=256 is divisible by 4). Shared memory for ConvBig is (128+128)*16*4B*4 stages = 64KB < 99KB/CTA limit.
3. Extend `run_conv_t` with an `int split_k` parameter and pass it as the last argument of `cutlass::conv::Conv2dProblemSize(..., cutlass::conv::Mode::kCrossCorrelation, split_k)`.
4. In `run_conv_t`, after `get_workspace_size`, zero the workspace before `initialize` (`wsb.zero_()` on the uint8 tensor) — CUTLASS serial split-k (SplitKMode::kSerial, the DefaultConv2dFprop default) uses a semaphore in workspace that must start at 0. For split_k==1 the zeroing is a no-op-sized buffer and costs nothing measurable.
5. Replace the body of `conv3x3` with a compile-time-instantiated, runtime-selected dispatch driven by M = N*H*W and the 170-SM wave criterion (target >= 340 CTAs = 2 full waves):
   - `long M = (long)N*H*W; long ctas_big = ((M+127)/128)*2; long ctas_small = ((M+127)/128)*4;`
   - if (ctas_big >= 340) -> run ConvBig with split_k=1;
   - else if (ctas_small >= 340) -> run ConvSmall with split_k=1;
   - else -> run ConvSmall with `split_k = (int)min(4L, (340 + ctas_small - 1)/ctas_small)` (>=2).
   Concrete outcomes for the scored shapes: 8x64x128 (M=65536) and 4x256x256 (M=262144) -> ConvBig; 1x131x131 (M=17161, ctas_big=270, ctas_small=540) -> ConvSmall split_k=1; 2x64x64 (M=8192, ctas_small=256) -> ConvSmall split_k=2 -> 512 CTAs (3 waves).
6. Make the selection safe: replace the hard `TORCH_CHECK(can_implement...)` for the ConvBig path with a check that, on failure, falls back to ConvSmall split_k=1 with the original TORCH_CHECKs, so no shape can fail to run.
7. Do not change the epilogue (alpha=1, beta=0, output NHWC into y1/y2), the tf32 pre-rounding of activations/weights, or the GN math; numerics must stay within max_atol 0.0028.
8. Verify after building: no local-memory spilling in the conv (registers/thread must stay <= 255 with 0 spill stores) and per-shape timing on all four shapes — if the mid or large shape does not improve with ConvBig, raise the ctas_big threshold so those shapes fall back to ConvSmall rather than regress.
strategy.evidence: Nsight Systems steady-state table: the CUTLASS ImplicitGemmConvolution is 86.6% of per-forward GPU time (20,264us over 24 launches = 844us/launch); everything else summed is 13.4%, so any non-conv round is Amdahl-capped at 13.4%. At 77.3 GFLOP per conv on the profiled shape, 844us = 91.6 TFLOPS = 87% of the 104.8 TFLOPS TF32 peak — little headroom there — but the per-shape table shows 2x256x64x64 at only 1.1188x vs 1.2409x for the mid shape; scaling the satellites linearly by pixel count (260us -> 32.5us) leaves ~147us per conv launch = ~65 TFLOPS ~= 62% of peak, and with a 128x64 tile that shape emits only ceil(8192/128)*4 = 256 CTAs for 170 SMs (1.5 waves). Section analysis supports wave quantization as a first-class limiter: NCU's SOLBottleneck OPT on gn_finalize/weight_krsc states 'This kernel grid is too small to fill the available resources on this device, resulting in only 0.25 full waves across all SMs.' Ruled out (secondary): DRAM bandwidth on our own elementwise kernels — gn_silu_add_nchw is at gpu__dram_throughput 88.83% and nchw2nhwc at 86.01%, i.e. already at the memory roof, yet they are 4.6% and 4.3% of steady time; moreover gn_partial moves 67MB in 17.5us = 3.8TB/s, above the 1.79TB/s DRAM peak, proving those passes are L2-resident rather than DRAM-limited, so the memory_bandwidth signature comes from kernels off the critical path. Departure from allowed_methods is deliberate: Own_And_Fuse_Vendor_Operator/KernelFusion can at best delete gn_partial (1.8%) and gn_silu_round (2.1%) — and the SiLU prologue fusion is blocked by the cp.async multistage mainloop — a ~4% ceiling versus the conv-side headroom above; the mechanism I use instead is threadblock-tile/split-k shape dispatch on the dominant operator.
strategy.expected_metric_change: Conv kernel duration down (mid shape 844us -> <=790us; 2x256x64x64 conv ~147us -> ~115us per launch), global/L2 load bytes per conv output down ~33% on ConvBig shapes ((128+128)*K vs (128+64)*K per tile => 54 -> 36 elements loaded per output, so lts__throughput and l1tex sector counts per conv drop), sm__inst_executed_pipe_tensor rate / achieved TF32 fraction up from ~87% toward >92%, and launch__waves_per_multiprocessor for the small shape up from ~1.5 to ~3.0 via split_k=2. Anti-regression: ConvBig must stay at 64KB shared memory per CTA (<99KB) with zero local-memory spilling requests and registers/thread <=255; the elementwise kernels must keep their current 86-89% DRAM throughput and unchanged launch shapes; if ConvBig or split-k does not beat the incumbent on any scored shape, that shape must fall back to the existing 128x64x16 split_k=1 config so no shape's geomean contribution regresses; the extra workspace zeroing must remain <1us.

strategy.bottleneck: The CUTLASS ImplicitGemm conv holds 86.7% of steady-state GPU time and runs at only ~75% of TF32 peak (~1953us vs 1475us roofline for the two convs); every satellite kernel is already at 85-89% of DRAM peak, so all remaining headroom is in the conv's tile/stage configuration.
strategy.optimisation method: Widen the owned conv's configuration space (add 3-stage 128x128x16 and 256x128x16 tiles) and replace the CTA-count heuristic with a one-time, per-shape measured pick over those tiles plus the existing split-k variants, keeping the current shape dispatch as fallback.
strategy.modification plan:
1. Leave all non-conv kernels (nchw2nhwc_round, gn_partial, gn_finalize, gn_silu_round, gn_silu_add_nchw, weight_krsc_round) and their launch shapes completely unchanged; they are already at DRAM roofline.
2. Add two new instantiations next to ConvSmall/ConvBig using the existing MakeConv template: `using ConvBigS3 = MakeConv<GemmShape<128,128,16>, GemmShape<64,64,16>, 3>::Op;` (smem drops from 64KB to 48KB, allowing 2 CTAs/SM on the 100KB SM instead of 1) and `using ConvWide = MakeConv<GemmShape<256,128,16>, GemmShape<64,64,16>, 3>::Op;` (8 warps, 72KB smem). Keep ConvSmall<128,64,16,4> and ConvBig<128,128,16,4> exactly as they are.
3. Refactor the call sites into one dispatcher `static bool launch_id(int id, int split_k, const float* xp, const float* wp, float* yp, int N,int H,int W,int C,int K, const torch::Tensor& proto, bool must_succeed)` that switches id 0->ConvSmall, 1->ConvBig, 2->ConvBigS3, 3->ConvWide and forwards to the existing run_conv_t<>.
4. FIRST COMPILABLE MILESTONE (do this before any autotune): in conv3x3, keep the existing ctas_big/ctas_small/target=340 logic but try id=2 first when ctas_big>=340, falling back to id=1, then to id=0 with the current split-k formula. Compile, run all four shapes, confirm numerical match (atol 2.8e-3) and record times. This alone preserves conv_config_shape_dispatch_splitk and should already win from the 1->2 CTA/SM change.
5. Then add the measured pick: a file-static `std::map<uint64_t,std::pair<int,int>> g_cfg;` keyed by ((uint64_t)N<<40)|(H<<20)|W (C=K=256 always).
6. On cache miss, build the candidate list {(2,1),(1,1),(3,1),(0,1),(0,2),(0,3),(0,4)}, drop any whose can_implement/initialize fails (use the must_succeed=false path already in run_conv_t), then time each with cudaEvent pairs on at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream(): 1 warmup launch + 3 timed launches, cudaStreamSynchronize, keep the minimum. Write the winning (id, split_k) into g_cfg. Timing runs on the real xn/w1r/y1 pointers of the current call, so no extra buffers are needed; y1 is fully overwritten by the final launch.
7. If the candidate list ends up empty (should not happen), fall back to the step-4 heuristic path with must_succeed=true.
8. After autotune, always execute exactly one conv launch with the cached (id, split_k) — do not leave the timing launches in the steady-state path; kernel launch count per forward must stay at its current value.
9. Autotune both conv1 and conv2 with the same cache entry (identical problem size), so the one-time cost is 7 candidates x 4 launches once per distinct shape.
10. Anti-regression checks: keep split-k candidates in the list so 2x64x64 (ctas_small=256<340) and 1x131x131 do not lose the accepted split-k mechanism; re-measure all four shapes and reject any config change that regresses any single shape, since the score is a geometric mean.
11. If turns run short, stop after step 4 (already a valid, correct kernel) and leave the autotune for the next round.

strategy.optimisation method: Decompose the forward along the batch axis into NC independent chunks and issue each chunk's full 9-kernel sequence on its own CUDA stream, so the DRAM-bound layout/GroupNorm/SiLU passes of one chunk execute concurrently with the compute-bound conv of another. Kernels themselves are unchanged.
strategy.modification plan:
1. Do NOT edit any __global__ kernel body, block size, or per-launch grid formula. All changes are confined to the host function `fused_block`.
2. Compute a chunk count from B only (every op in the block is independent per batch element): `int NC = (B>=4 && B%4==0) ? 4 : ((B>=2 && B%2==0) ? 2 : 1);`. Concrete: B=8 -> 4 chunks of 2; B=4 -> 4 chunks of 1; B=2 -> 2 chunks of 1; B=1 -> NC=1. When NC==1 execute exactly the present code path (no streams, no events) so the 1x256x131x131 shape is untouched.
3. MILESTONE 1 (must compile and match reference before anything else): keep a single stream and simply wrap the existing body in `for (int c=0;c<NC;++c)`, with `int b0 = c*(B/NC), Bc = B/NC;` and every pointer offset by `(long)b0*CH*(long)HW` for x/xn/y1/z1/y2/out and by `(long)b0*CH` for scale/shift; pass `Bc` wherever `B` was passed (grid.z of nchw2nhwc_round and gn_silu_add_nchw, grid.y of gn_silu_round/gn_partial/gn_finalize, and N of `conv3x3`). Allocate xn, y1, z1, y2, out, scale, shift ONCE at full size before the loop. Verify numerics (chunking is bit-exact: GroupNorm reduces over (n,group) only, conv has no cross-batch reuse, residual is elementwise).
4. Hoist the two `weight_krsc_round_kernel` launches and `w1r`/`w2r` allocation OUT of the chunk loop; they run once on the entering stream before the loop.
5. MILESTONE 2 (the actual win): obtain NC streams once per call via `at::cuda::getStreamFromPool()` into a small stack array. Create an `at::cuda::CUDAEvent start_ev`, record it on the entering stream after step 4, and call `start_ev.block(streams[c])` for each c so every side stream waits for the allocations and the rounded weights.
6. Inside the chunk loop, open `at::cuda::CUDAStreamGuard guard(streams[c]);` before the launches. This makes `at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream()` inside `gn_stats`, `run_conv_t` (both the CUTLASS `op(stream)` call and its workspace `torch::empty`) and the raw `<<<...>>>` launches resolve to the side stream with no signature changes.
7. After the loop, for each c record an `at::cuda::CUDAEvent end_ev[c]` on streams[c] and call `end_ev[c].block(at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream())` on the entering stream, then return `out`. This join makes it safe for the caching allocator that x/out/xn were allocated on the entering stream and used on side streams.
8. Keep the psum/psq temporaries allocated inside `gn_stats` (they are now per-chunk and allocated under the stream guard, so they stay on their own stream's pool).
9. Do not add any in-place write, device transfer, or change to `get_inputs()`.
10. Verify after building: (a) all four scored shapes still pass tolerance; (b) nsys shows conv kernels overlapping nchw2nhwc/gn_silu_* in time; (c) if the 2x256x64x64 shape regresses (its per-chunk conv grid is only 128 CTAs), tighten step 2 to require `(long)Bc*H*W >= 8192` before allowing NC>1, which drops that shape back to NC=1.
11. Next round, if this lands, raise NC to 8 for B=8 and consider splitting along H with a 1-row halo so B=1 shapes can also pipeline.

Per-kernel gpu__time_duration of nchw2nhwc/gn_silu_* will INCREASE (they now share bandwidth) - this is expected and is not a regression; only end-to-end time counts. strategy.bottleneck: [compute/L2-traffic bound] The CUTLASS ImplicitGemmConvolution mainloop is 85.8% of steady per-forward GPU time (31,794us / 96 launches). It runs one hardcoded 128x64x16 threadblock tile; the narrow 64-wide N tile forces each activation K-slice to be re-fetched 4x (N/N_tile=256/64) through L2, so the conv sits at ~88% of TF32 roofline on the mid shape and lower on the 256x256 shape. All satellites together are only 14.2%.
strategy.primary_optimisation_method: Threadblock tile-geometry retune of the CUTLASS conv mainloop: add a 128x128x16 (warp 64x64, 3-stage) instantiation and dispatch to it whenever M=N*H*W gives >=2 full CTA waves, keeping the existing 128x64x16 config for small-M shapes. Algebraically identical output; halves activation L2->SMEM re-fetch (N/N_tile 4->2) and doubles MACs per loaded fragment, which is the work/traffic term limiting the 85.8% hot kernel. Amdahl cap is 85.8%, versus 14.2% for any satellite fusion.
strategy.modification_plan:
SMEM BUDGET CHECK (mandatory, conv-like target): new tile 128x128x16 tf32, bytes_per_stage = (128+128)*16*4 = 16 KB; 3 stages = 48 KB <= 99 KB per-block limit and 2 CTAs/SM = 96 KB <= 100 KB per SM. PASSES. No custom smem staging is introduced; CUTLASS iterators already give coalesced 128-bit NHWC loads (alignment 4), so the coalescing-first rule is satisfied by construction.

1. In the CUDA source, keep `MakeConv` unchanged and add a second instantiation next to the existing one inside `conv3x3`:
   `using ConvBig = typename MakeConv<cutlass::gemm::GemmShape<128,128,16>, cutlass::gemm::GemmShape<64,64,16>, 3>::Op;`
   and keep `using ConvSmall = typename MakeConv<GemmShape<128,64,16>, GemmShape<64,32,16>, 4>::Op;` (today's config, bit-identical path for small shapes).
2. Replace the single call in `conv3x3` with an exact dispatch on CTA count:
   `long M = (long)N*H*W; long ctas_big = ((M+127)/128) * 2; if (ctas_big >= 340) run_conv_t<ConvBig>(...); else run_conv_t<ConvSmall>(...);`
   340 = 2 waves x 170 SMs. This routes 8x64x128 (1024 CTAs) and 4x256x256 (4096 CTAs) to the 128x128 tile, and keeps 2x64x64 (128 CTAs) and 1x131x131 (268 CTAs) on the current 128x64 tile so those two shapes cannot regress. Note the dispatch must use the CHUNK batch `Bc`, not `B`, since streams split the batch.
3. Leave `run_conv_t` templated exactly as-is; it already takes the Op as a template parameter, so no other code changes. Keep `IteratorAlgorithm::kOptimized`, `LinearCombination<float,4,float,float>`, alignment 4,4, and the Sm80 op class (TF32 in, fp32 accumulate) — precision class is unchanged.
4. Verify `can_implement` for ConvBig at every scored shape (it is already TORCH_CHECKed); if it ever fails, fall through to ConvSmall instead of aborting: wrap the big call in a status test and re-run with ConvSmall on failure.
5. Preserve the accepted `concurrent_stream_batch_decomposition` mechanism verbatim: the dispatch lives entirely inside `conv3x3`, which is called from both the NC==1 path and the per-chunk loop under `CUDAStreamGuard`; do not hoist any state out of `conv3x3`, and keep the per-call workspace `torch::empty` so the two streams do not share a workspace buffer. Confirm after the edit that stream count, event pattern and the 456 launch total are unchanged.
6. Build and correctness-check all four shapes against `_ref` (max_atol budget 0.0027-0.003). Numerics are unaffected by tile shape apart from K-accumulation order inside a fixed K=2304 loop, which is unchanged (no split-K introduced).
7. Time each shape separately. Accept only if 8x64x128 and 4x256x256 improve and the other two are unchanged (they take the identical old code path).
8. If 128x128x16/3-stage underperforms on 4x256x256, try, in order and one at a time: stages 4 (64 KB, 1 CTA/SM), then warp shape 64x32 with 256 threads. Do not add split-K, do not change the epilogue, and do not touch any satellite kernel this round — they hold only 14.2% combined.
9. Keep `weight_krsc_round_kernel`, `nchw2nhwc_round_kernel`, `gn_*` kernels and the NC chunk heuristic byte-identical so the only variable measured is tile geometry.
